script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Family
Theme: second chances

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. SMITH LIVING ROOM - DAY

MRS. SMITH (50s, kind, warm) sits next to her husband, MR. SMITH (60s, gruff, distant). They share an awkward silence.

MRS. SMITH
(gently)
George, we need to talk.

MR. SMITH
(grumbles)
What about?

MRS. SMITH
(sighs)
About our son, Ben. I've been thinking... I believe it's time for us to reach out to him again.

MR. SMITH
(angrily)
Are you nuts? That boy screwed up. He walked out on us and his sister, left us all broken. I don't want anything to do with him.

MRS. SMITH
(tears welling up)
But, George, he's our son. And he's been through so much since then. He's not the same boy who left us. He's grown up, made mistakes, and now he's trying to make amends. Don't we deserve a second chance?

MR. SMITH
(sighs)
Fine. I'll consider it. But that's all I can promise.

INT. BEN'S APARTMENT - NIGHT

Ben (30s, troubled, regretful) sits alone, staring at an old family photo. He dials his parents' number.

BEN
(nervously)
Hi, it's me, Ben. I was wondering if I could see you both sometime soon. I have something important to discuss with you.

INT. SMITH KITCHEN - DAY

Mrs. Smith answers the call. Her eyes fill with hope and tears.

MRS. SMITH
(excitedly)
Ben! Oh, my dear, it's so good to hear your voice. Yes, we'd love to see you. When can you come over?

INT. PARK BENCH - DAY

Ben meets his parents for the first time in years. They exchange pleasantries and share stories about their lives.

MR. SMITH
(seriously)
Ben, I'd like to talk to you about something important.

BEN
(nervously)
Yes, Dad. What is it?

MR. SMITH
(sighs)
Your mother and I have been talking about our past. About you. We both want to give you another chance. But, we need to know that you're willing to make things right between us.

BEN
(tearfully)
Yes, I am. I've made so many mistakes, but I've learned from them. I've grown up and I'm not the same person I was before. I'm ready to make amends and be a part of our family again.

MR. SMITH
(pauses, then nods)
Alright, Ben. We'll give it a try.

INT. SMITH LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

The family gathers around the table for dinner. They laugh, share stories, and enjoy each other's company.

MRS. SMITH
(smiling)
George, I'm so glad we gave Ben a second chance. It feels like we've been given a second chance as well.

MR. SMITH
(smiling)
I agree. It's good to have our family whole again.

INT. SMITH GARDEN - DAY

Ben, Mrs. Smith, and a young girl (BEN'S NIECE, 8) play in the garden. The sun sets as they enjoy the moment, creating memories that will last a lifetime.

BEN
(looking at his niece)
Mom, this feels right. I'm so grateful for this second chance.

MRS. SMITH
(smiling)
We're just glad you're here, Ben. And we'll always be here for you.

FADE OUT.

END OF SCREENPLAY.
